rows.note: This is the all-purpose word for elastic material and elastic bands, including a hair tie when the context is clear.

example.english: The elastic in these trousers is loose, so I keep having to pull them up.
example.traditional: 條褲嘅橡筋鬆咗，成日要拉返上去。
example.jyutping: tiu4 fu3 ge3 zoeng6 gan1 sung1 zo2 seng4 jat6 jiu3 laai1 faan2 soeng5 heoi3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something that stretches and returns to its original shape.

example.english: This rubber band is elastic and returns to its original length after being stretched.
example.traditional: 呢條橡筋有彈性，拉長咗都會縮返。
example.jyutping: ne1 tiu4 zoeng6 gan1 jau5 daan6 sing3 laai1 coeng4 zo2 dou1 wui6 suk1 faan2

rows.note: Use it before an item noun when the material or clothing feature is elastic, such as in 橡筋褲.

example.english: I bought a pair of elastic-waisted trousers that do not feel tight around my waist when I run.
example.traditional: 我買咗條橡筋褲，跑步嗰陣唔會箍住條腰。
example.jyutping: ngo5 maai5 zo2 tiu4 zoeng6 gan1 fu3 paau2 bou6 go2 zan6 m4 wui5 ku1 zyu6 tiu4 jiu1

rows.note: Use this when you specifically mean a ring-shaped hair tie rather than elastic in general.

example.english: I can't find an elastic, so I'll leave my hair down.
example.traditional: 我搵唔到髮圈，唯有放低頭髮。
example.jyutping: ngo5 wan2 m4 dou3 faat3 hyun1 wai4 jau5 fong3 dai1 tau4 faat3

rows.jyutping: deoi3 gaa3 gaak3 bin3 faa3 man5 gam2
rows.note: Use this in economic contexts when demand reacts strongly to changes in price.

example.english: Demand for this kind of product is elastic, so even a small price cut brings in more buyers.
example.traditional: 呢類產品嘅需求對價格變化敏感，減少少價就多人買。
example.jyutping: ni1 leoi6 caan2 ban2 ge3 seoi1 kau4 deoi3 gaa3 gaak3 bin3 faa3 man5 gam2 gaam2 siu2 siu2 gaa3 zau6 do1 jan4 maai5
